# List Item

One row in a List: a line of text, an optional second line, slots at either end, and optionally a link, a button, or secondary actions.

**Not implemented yet.** This page is the *approved intent* — the props API signed off at gate 1 of the build order, before any React exists. Do not import it; there is nothing to import.

| | |
|---|---|
| Registry name | `list-item` |
| Family | content |
| Tier | free |
| Status (css / react / figma) | future / future / future |
| Depends on | `state-layer`, `icon`, `menu`, `menu-item`, `button` |

## Behavior

An `<li>` holding the row's content, and — when interactive — one real `<a>` or `<button>` stretched over it. Secondary actions are data, rendered as a Menu behind a trailing button. No primitive: a row in the normal tab order has no keyboard model to own.

- **A row is a link, a button, or neither — decided by `href` and `onClick`** — `href` makes the row an `<a>`; `onClick` alone makes it a `<button type="button">`; both makes it a link with the click intercepted, the bargain TopNav and SideNav make for client-side routing. Neither makes it static content. The element is never the `<li>` itself with `role="button"` bolted on — a list item that pretends to be a button loses its list position, and a real element gets keyboard activation, middle-click and the links list for free.
- **The whole row is the target, through one stretched element** — The link or button wraps only the text, and a pseudo-element stretches its hit area over the row. Wrapping the entire row in an `<a>` instead would put the description, the trailing badge and any control inside the link — so the accessible name becomes everything in the row read together, and a Switch inside a link is an interactive element nested in another, which is invalid and unpredictable. Stretching keeps the name to the row's text and leaves room beside it for a control that is not part of the link.
- **The description is a description, not part of the name** — The row's text is the accessible name; `description` is joined by `aria-describedby`. A screen reader's links list then reads 'Quiet hours' rather than 'Quiet hours 10 pm – 7 am', and twenty rows remain distinguishable by name alone. The description is still read when the row is focused, so nothing is lost.
- **`trailing` is for one thing, and an interactive row cannot hold a control there** — A trailing slot holds metadata — a Badge, a timestamp — or one control, such as a Switch on a settings row. A row that is both a link and holds a Switch has two targets on one line with nothing to tell a thumb which it will hit, and the stretched link would sit under the switch. The type cannot see what is inside a ReactNode, so this is a contract rule: a row with `href` or `onClick` takes metadata in `trailing` and nothing interactive. Its secondary commands go in `actions`, which is built to sit beside a stretched link.
- **Secondary actions are data, and they are always reachable without a gesture** — Swipe actions were proposed as their own component and declined; this prop is what replaced them. `actions` takes `{ label: string; icon?: LucideIcon; destructive?: boolean; onSelect: () => void }[]` and renders them, always, as a Menu behind a trailing icon-only Button — the keyboard, switch-access and screen-reader path, and the pointer path on a desktop. A swipe that reveals the same actions is a future enhancement over this same array, which is the point of it being data: a gesture can then never hold an action the menu does not, and the non-gesture equivalent is not a fallback someone has to remember to add — it is the default rendering.
- **No swipe gesture in this version** — Sheet's contract declined drag-to-dismiss for reasons that apply here unchanged: a horizontal swipe is a pointer state machine with a distance and velocity threshold, it competes with the browser's own back-swipe on iOS Safari and with horizontal scrolling in the row's container, and it must be reversible before release. That is a primitive — a pure reducer over pointer positions, no DOM — proposed through gate 1 on its own, not a styling detail riding along with the row. When it ships, a full swipe must never complete a destructive action without an undo.
- **The actions button is named after its row** — Twenty rows each with a button called 'More actions' produce a screen-reader button list of twenty identical entries. The trigger is named by `aria-labelledby` pointing at both its own `actionsLabel` text and the row's text, so it reads 'More actions, Invoice 42' — the row tells the reader which one it is without the caller writing twenty strings.
- **Disabled blocks the row and its actions, and keeps both reachable** — `disabled` puts `aria-disabled` on the row's link or button and on the actions trigger, and the click guard blocks both; neither leaves the tab order, so a reader can still find out the row exists and why it cannot be used. A row disabled while its actions still work is a row whose most important command is unavailable and whose secondary ones are not, which is a state worth not being able to express.
- **Token gap: size.target.min — needs the design-tokens skill** — A row is a thumb target on a phone and should be at least 44–48px tall. The recipe composes `size.control.lg` plus `space.1-5` on each side as a stand-in, because the size scale stops at 36px and the 48px step that exists, `space.12`, is spacing. One `size.target.min` token closes this here, in BottomNav, in FAB and in Chip.
- **Open: the focus ring at a list's inline edges** — An edge-to-edge row's ring sits outside the row, by `focus.ring-offset`, which is outside the list's inline edges. List pads its block edges so the first and last rings survive a scroll container, but padding the inline edges would inset every row from the page's edge and undo 'edge-to-edge'. Either the rule is that an edge-to-edge list is never an overflow-clipping container, or a row's ring is drawn inset (a negative offset of `focus.ring-width` plus `focus.ring-offset`) — which keeps the gap and the width this system requires but moves the ring inside the target. That choice belongs at gate 2.
- **Web and native** — On the web it renders `<li>`, with an `<a href>` or `<button type="button">` over the text when interactive, `aria-describedby` to the description, and `aria-disabled` when disabled. The actions trigger is an icon-only Button with `aria-haspopup="menu"` opening a Menu. On React Native it renders a `View` (or a `Pressable` with `accessibilityRole="link"` or `"button"` when interactive), `accessibilityHint` from the description, and `accessibilityState={{ disabled }}`. `actions` become the row's `accessibilityActions`, with `onAccessibilityAction` dispatching to each `onSelect` — so VoiceOver's actions rotor and TalkBack's actions menu reach them from the row itself — and the visible trailing button remains for touch. A future swipe reveals the same array on both platforms. Web-only: `href`, `onClick` (a DOM `MouseEvent`) and `className`; the native package takes `onPress` in their place. No prop is native-only. Rata-drawn (decision N5): the row is a drawn `View` or `Pressable` from the same recipe, not an OS table cell. The native implementation ships in the pro tier (decision N6).

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | The row's text — what the row is. |
| `description?` | `ReactNode` | — | A second, secondary line under the text. |
| `leading?` | `ReactNode` | — | A visual at the start of the row — an Icon or an Avatar. |
| `trailing?` | `ReactNode` | — | Metadata or one control at the end of the row. |
| `href?` | `string` | — | Makes the row a link to this address. |
| `onClick?` | `(event: MouseEvent<HTMLElement>) => void` | — | Makes the row a button, or — with `href` — intercepts the link for client-side routing. |
| `actions?` | `ListItemAction[]` | — | Secondary commands on this row — `{ label: string; icon?: LucideIcon; destructive?: boolean; onSelect: () => void }` each — shown in a Menu behind a trailing button. |
| `actionsLabel?` | `string` | `"More actions"` | The visible-to-assistive-technology name of the actions trigger, before the row's own text. |
| `disabled?` | `boolean` | — | Blocks the row's activation and its actions, while keeping both focusable and announced. |
| `className?` | `string` | — | Extra classes on the `<li>`, for placement — not for restyling it. |

### `children`

```ts
children: ReactNode
```

The row's text — what the row is.

**Use when**

- A short label: a name, a title, a setting.

**Don't use for**

- Two lines run together. The second line is `description`, so it can be styled and announced as secondary.

**Accessibility** The accessible name of the row's link or button, and the only thing in it.

### `description`

```ts
description?: ReactNode
```

A second, secondary line under the text.

**Use when**

- The value of a setting ('10 pm – 7 am'), a message preview, a file's size and date.

**Don't use for**

- The row's only meaningful text. If the description is what tells rows apart, it is the text.

**Accessibility** Joined by `aria-describedby`: read on focus, kept out of the name.

### `leading`

```ts
leading?: ReactNode
```

A visual at the start of the row — an Icon or an Avatar.

**Use when**

- An Avatar for a person, an Icon for a kind of thing.
- A Checkbox, for a list whose rows can be selected for a bulk action — on a row that is not itself a link or button.

**Don't use for**

- An image that carries information the text does not. The slot is decorative by default, and a meaning that only exists in it is lost to anyone not looking.

**Accessibility** Should be decorative — an Icon with no `label`, an Avatar with `decorative` — because the row's text already names it.

### `trailing`

```ts
trailing?: ReactNode
```

Metadata or one control at the end of the row.

**Use when**

- A Badge, a count, a timestamp.
- One Switch on a settings row that is not itself a link.

**Don't use for**

- A control on a row with `href` or `onClick` — two targets on one line. Put commands in `actions` instead.
- Several buttons. That is `actions`, which collapses them into one trigger.

**Accessibility** Read after the row's text, in DOM order. A control placed here needs its own accessible name; a Switch's `label` can repeat the row's text with `labelHidden`.

### `href`

```ts
href?: string
```

Makes the row a link to this address.

**Use when**

- A row that opens the thing it describes.

**Don't use for**

- `href="#"` to make a row clickable. A row that performs an action rather than going somewhere takes `onClick` alone and becomes a button.

**Accessibility** Renders an `<a>`, so the row is in the links list and announced as a link.

### `onClick`

```ts
onClick?: (event: MouseEvent<HTMLElement>) => void
```

Makes the row a button, or — with `href` — intercepts the link for client-side routing.

**Use when**

- A row that opens a Sheet or a Dialog in place.
- With `href`, a router's navigate call.

**Don't use for**

- Selecting the row as an answer. That is RadioGroup.

**Accessibility** Alone, renders a `<button type="button">`, activated by Enter and Space. With `href`, it stays a link.

### `actions`

```ts
actions?: ListItemAction[]
```

Secondary commands on this row — `{ label: string; icon?: LucideIcon; destructive?: boolean; onSelect: () => void }` each — shown in a Menu behind a trailing button.

**Use when**

- Archive, rename, share, delete — what a mobile app would put behind a swipe.

**Don't use for**

- The row's primary action. That is the row itself, via `href` or `onClick`.
- One action that every row has and every reader uses. A command that common belongs on the row's own page or in a toolbar, not one tap deep in every row.

**Accessibility** The trigger is named '`actionsLabel`, <row text>'. Each action becomes a MenuItem, and `destructive` becomes MenuItem's `destructive`.

### `actionsLabel`

```ts
actionsLabel?: string = "More actions"
```

The visible-to-assistive-technology name of the actions trigger, before the row's own text.

**Use when**

- A translated string.

**Don't use for**

- Repeating the row's text in it. The row's text is already appended.

**Accessibility** One part of the trigger's `aria-labelledby`; the row's text is the other.

### `disabled`

```ts
disabled?: boolean
```

Blocks the row's activation and its actions, while keeping both focusable and announced.

**Use when**

- A row that exists but cannot be opened right now — a file still uploading.

**Don't use for**

- A static row. A row with no `href`, `onClick` or `actions` has nothing to disable.

**Accessibility** `aria-disabled`, not the `disabled` attribute, on the link or button and the actions trigger.

### `className`

```ts
className?: string
```

Extra classes on the `<li>`, for placement — not for restyling it.

**Use when**

- Rare. The row's spacing and states are the component's.

**Don't use for**

- Removing the divider on one row. That is List's `dividers`, and a list where some rows are divided reads as two lists.

## Use cases

### A row that opens a page

The commonest row: a thing in a collection, which the reader taps to see in full.

```tsx
<ListItem
  href="/people/ada"
  leading={<Avatar name="Ada Lovelace" decorative />}
  description="Last seen 2 hours ago"
>
  Ada Lovelace
</ListItem>
```

The Avatar is decorative because the text names the person. The link's name is 'Ada Lovelace'; the last-seen line is its description.

### A row with secondary actions

A message or file row where archive and delete are a mobile app's swipe actions.

```tsx
<ListItem
  href={`/mail/${message.id}`}
  description={message.preview}
  actions={[
    { label: "Archive", icon: Archive, onSelect: () => archive(message.id) },
    { label: "Delete", icon: Trash2, destructive: true, onSelect: () => remove(message.id) },
  ]}
>
  {message.subject}
</ListItem>
```

The actions render as a Menu behind a trailing button named 'More actions, <subject>'. That is the path for keyboard, switch access and screen readers today, and it stays the path when a swipe gesture is added over the same array.

### A setting with a switch

A settings row whose control is the whole point, and the row itself goes nowhere.

```tsx
<ListItem trailing={<Switch label="Dark mode" labelHidden checked={dark} onCheckedChange={setDark} />}>
  Dark mode
</ListItem>
```

No `href` or `onClick`, so the row is static and the Switch is its only target. The Switch's `label` repeats the row's text because it is the switch's own name.

### Reaching for the wrong component: a row that is two targets

A row that opens a page and also carries a toggle.

```tsx
<ListItem href="/settings/wifi" trailing={<Switch label="Wi-Fi" labelHidden checked={wifi} onCheckedChange={setWifi} />}>
  Wi-Fi
</ListItem>
```

Don't. The stretched link lies under the switch, and a thumb aiming at either has nothing to tell it which it will hit. Make the row static with the Switch, and put a separate 'Wi-Fi networks' row with the `href` below it.

## Token recipe

### base

One row. Leading slot, text, trailing slot, in that order along the inline axis; the text column takes the slack.

| Property | Token |
|---|---|
| min-block-size | `size.control.lg plus space.1-5 above and below (48px) — a stand-in for the touch-target minimum this system has no token for; see the token-gap decision` |
| padding-block | `space.padding.xs` |
| padding-inline | `space.padding.md — and max(space.padding.md, env(safe-area-inset-left / right)) when the list is edge-to-edge, so a phone in landscape does not put the text under the notch` |
| gap between slots and text | `space.gap.md` |
| text color | `theme.fg.primary` |
| text font-size | `type.body.size` |
| text font-weight | `type.body.weight` |
| text line-height | `type.body.line-height` |
| gap between text and description | `space.stack.2xs` |
| description color | `theme.fg.secondary` |
| description font-size | `type.supporting.size` |
| description line-height | `type.supporting.line-height` |
| leading icon size | `size.icon.md` |
| leading icon colour | `theme.fg.secondary` |
| trailing text colour | `theme.fg.secondary` |

### divider

A rule above every row but the first, drawn by the row so a conditional row never leaves a doubled or orphaned line.

| Property | Token |
|---|---|
| border-block-start | `border.default solid theme.border.default` |
| inset | `starts at the text column when the row has a leading slot, so the rule does not cut between an avatar and its own text` |

### interactive

A row with `href` or `onClick`. The link or button is stretched over the whole row, so the whole row is the target.

| Property | Token |
|---|---|
| hover / press | `compose the .rata-state-layer class on the row` |
| focus ring | `theme.focus-ring at focus.ring-width, offset focus.ring-offset, on :focus-visible — drawn around the row, which is the target the reader is about to activate` |
| disclosure chevron | `size.icon.sm, theme.fg.muted — decorative, and shown only for href rows, since it promises a new page` |
| disabled | `state.disabled-opacity, on aria-disabled` |

### actions

The trailing control that opens a row's secondary actions. Above the stretched link in the stacking order, so pressing it does not also follow the row.

| Property | Token |
|---|---|
| target inline-size / block-size | `size.control.md` |
| glyph size | `size.icon.md` |
| glyph colour | `theme.fg.secondary` |
| border-radius | `radius.element` |
| hover / press | `compose the .rata-state-layer class` |
| focus ring | `theme.focus-ring at focus.ring-width, offset focus.ring-offset, on :focus-visible` |
